question: The experiment left context-menu.tsx and alert-dialog.tsx composing Base UI parts out of react-aria-components imports. Can they be rebuilt onto Base UI 1.7.0's NATIVE @base-ui/react/context-menu and @base-ui/react/alert-dialog without moving the public API — and how many of the other 64 non-rebuilt components are half-migrated the same way?
verdict: The two files were the whole defect and both are now native, but the two halves of the answer are not symmetric. CONTEXT-MENU is a clean win: Base UI's ContextMenu.Root renders a Menu.Root underneath, so menu.tsx composes into it UNCHANGED, the three hand-built mechanisms the React Aria version needed (portaled anchor div, PopoverContext triggerRef override, PressResponder) all delete, and the suite goes 0/4 → 3/4 with the one remaining failure pinning a workaround the engine made unnecessary. ALERT-DIALOG passes 4/4 but is only PARTIALLY native, and that is the finding worth carrying forward: Base UI's alert dialog is a ROOT-level component and Lumo's public API already spent the root (DialogTrigger) and the popup (DialogModal) on the plain dialog, so AlertDialog.Root and AlertDialog.Popup have nowhere to go. THE HUNT FOUND NOTHING ELSE THAT THROWS. Ten further files mix a runtime react-aria-components import with a rebuilt sibling, and every one of them renders — because in all ten the rebuilt sibling is either a pure cva export (classnames, no engine) or a Base UI component that needs no context of its own. The throwing class was exactly two files, and it was context, not mixing: a Base UI part rendered outside its Root.

method.throw_test: Each candidate rendered through its covering suite (renderToStaticMarkup + @testing-library/react render). file-upload, hover-card and search-field have NO covering suite in the repository, so a throwaway probe file rendered all three under fa-IR in both arms and was DELETED after the result was recorded — 6/6 passed, no throw.
method.typecheck: npx tsc --noEmit in packages/ui — 2 errors, both pre-existing and both in probe test files (probe.state-vocabulary.test.tsx:135, probe2.state-vocabulary.test.tsx:30, TS2741 TabListProps.label). ZERO errors in any component file.
method.tests: Individual suites plus one full `vitest run` of packages/ui. NOT ONE TEST FILE WAS EDITED.
method.not_run: pnpm run verify, next build — RAM budget, per brief. The Integrate agent owns the one verify.

context-menu.before: imported MenuTrigger, PopoverContext, MenuTriggerProps, PopoverProps from react-aria-components AND MenuPopover/Menu from the Base UI menu.tsx
context-menu.after: @base-ui/react/context-menu — ContextMenu.Root + ContextMenu.Trigger; zero react-aria-components imports of any kind, type or runtime
context-menu.why_it_composes: ContextMenuRoot renders <MenuRootContext.Provider value={undefined}><Menu.Root/></MenuRootContext.Provider>, so every part menu.tsx uses (Menu.Portal/Positioner/Popup/Item/Group/GroupLabel/Separator/SubmenuRoot/SubmenuTrigger) finds its context unchanged. ContextMenu.Portal/.Positioner/.Popup/.Item are literal re-exports of the same Menu.* modules in the dist — composing menu.tsx IS the native composition.
context-menu.public_api: unchanged. ContextMenuTriggerProps was `Omit<AriaMenuTriggerProps, 'children'|'trigger'|'isOpen'|'defaultOpen'>` + children, which resolves to exactly { children, onOpenChange }. That shape is now stated literally, so the RAC type dependency is gone without the surface moving.
deleted_mechanisms: the portaled 1-point [data-lumo-context-menu-anchor] div — Base UI's anchor is a virtual object with getBoundingClientRect(), never a node
React Aria's PressResponder dev warning ('no pressable child registered') the old header had to apologise for
the two unreachable aria-label="Dismiss" sentinels — an open Lumo context menu now announces ZERO English
context-menu.added: one onKeyDown that re-dispatches a native contextmenu MouseEvent at the focused element's centre. Browsers already map Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key to that event; jsdom does not, so without this the documented keyboard path is untestable. It routes into Base UI's own handler — it is not a second open path.

alert-dialog.before: imported Dialog as AriaDialog + DialogProps from react-aria-components and rendered <AriaDialog role="alertdialog"> inside the Base UI dialog.tsx overlay/modal
alert-dialog.after: @base-ui/react/alert-dialog — AlertDialog.Close for both verbs, Dialog.Title (via DialogHeading) for the name; react-aria-components remains as a TYPE-ONLY import for DialogProps, the same construction dialog.tsx and tooltip.tsx already use and which is erased at build
alert-dialog.public_api: unchanged. Same exports (AlertDialog, AlertDialogTone, AlertDialogProps, alertDialogFooterVariants), same required strings (title, confirmLabel, cancelLabel), same tone variants, same absence of closeLabel.

THE_NATIVE_ROOT_IS_AT_THE_WRONG_LAYER.severity: unresolved — needs an API decision, not a code fix
THE_NATIVE_ROOT_IS_AT_THE_WRONG_LAYER.finding: AlertDialog.Root is `useRenderDialogRoot('alert-dialog', props)`, i.e. Dialog.Root in alert-dialog mode. EVERYTHING the role means lives in that root's store: `role: 'alertdialog'` is read back by AlertDialog.Popup off `store.useState('role')`, and `disablePointerDismissal` is forced true by the mode. The other seven exported parts (Backdrop, Close, Description, Popup, Portal, Title, Viewport) are not alert-dialog components at all — index.parts.js re-exports the IDENTICAL Dialog.* modules under alert-dialog names.
THE_NATIVE_ROOT_IS_AT_THE_WRONG_LAYER.why_it_cannot_be_adopted: Lumo's public API composes an alert dialog out of DialogTrigger → DialogOverlay → DialogModal → AlertDialog. DialogTrigger is already Dialog.Root and DialogModal is already Dialog.Popup. AlertDialog.Root has nowhere to go because the caller never writes an alert-dialog root. AlertDialog.Popup cannot be rendered here either: it calls useDialogRootContext() non-optionally (it would bind to the PLAIN dialog root above it, whose role is 'dialog'), registers itself as that root's popupElement — clobbering DialogModal's registration — and wraps itself in a second FloatingFocusManager against the same floatingRootContext.
THE_NATIVE_ROOT_IS_AT_THE_WRONG_LAYER.what_was_done_instead: The body element declares role="alertdialog" itself and mints its own title id with useId(), passed to Dialog.Title's `id` prop (which syncs it into the root store, so the outer DialogModal is labelled by the same heading — one <h2>, one id, two elements pointing at it). Both verbs are AlertDialog.Close.
what_it_costs: outside-press dismissal stays ON, because the mode that forces disablePointerDismissal is unreachable — a native root would have fixed this for free, and it is the exact behaviour the component's own docblock forbids
the tree carries a role="alertdialog" element nested inside a role="dialog" element
AlertDialog used OUTSIDE a DialogTrigger still throws 'Base UI: DialogRootContext is missing' from Dialog.Title — unchanged from the pre-rewrite state and not fixable without the root
THE_NATIVE_ROOT_IS_AT_THE_WRONG_LAYER.the_fix_that_is_not_allowed_here: give alert dialogs their own AlertDialogTrigger/AlertDialogOverlay/AlertDialogModal mapped onto AlertDialog.Root/Portal+Backdrop/Popup. That is a public API change and this experiment may not make one.

one_trap_worth_recording.name: alert-dialog.close-onclick-vs-onpress
one_trap_worth_recording.finding: `onConfirm` MUST sit on the AlertDialog.Close, not on the Button inside its `render`. Lumo's Button sets its onClick from `onPress` and then spreads `...rest` AFTER it, so an onClick merged in from a Base UI `render` lands in rest and REPLACES the onPress-derived handler rather than chaining with it. Put onPress on a rendered Button and the callback is dropped silently — no type error, no warning.
one_trap_worth_recording.generalises_to: every Base UI part with a `render` prop that merges an event handler onto a Lumo Button: Dialog.Close, Menu.Trigger, Popover.Trigger, Select.Trigger, Tooltip.Trigger.

test_results.before: 2 passed / 2 failed — (1) aria-labelledby was null, because RAC's HeadingContext no longer exists and DialogHeading's id went to the OUTER Dialog.Popup; (2) neither verb closed, because RAC's render-prop `close` was bound to a RAC dialog state nothing drives any more
test_results.note: Both former failures were the mixed composition, not the assertions. Nothing was weakened.

the_hunt.criterion: a non-rebuilt component that imports a rebuilt sibling (button, switch, checkbox, toggle, select, menu, combobox, dialog, popover, tooltip, tabs, slider, number-field, context-menu, alert-dialog) AND imports react-aria-components
the_hunt.headline: The brief's hypothesis — 'any file that mixes the two will throw the same way' — is FALSIFIED for all ten. Mixing is not the defect. The defect was rendering a Base UI PART outside its Base UI ROOT, and that is a property of which symbols are imported, not of whether two libraries appear in the same file.
the_hunt.the_real_predicate: throws ⟺ the file renders a Base UI part whose use*RootContext() call is non-optional, without that root in its ancestry. All ten below fail this test: seven import only a cva/const export from the rebuilt sibling (classnames, zero engine), and three import a rebuilt COMPONENT that is context-free on its own (Base UI's Button and Checkbox both render standalone).

files.mixed_import: runtime `{ Autocomplete, Collection, Header, Input, Menu, MenuItem, MenuSection, SearchField, Separator, Text, composeRenderProps, useFilter }` from react-aria-components + `{ Dialog, DialogHeading, DialogModal, DialogOverlay, DialogTrigger }` from ./dialog.tsx
files.why_not: DialogTrigger is itself Dialog.Root, so the four Base UI dialog parts it imports arrive WITH their root — the composition is self-contained. The RAC Autocomplete/Menu tree inside is likewise self-contained RAC. Two engines, one document, no shared context.
files.native_replacement: @base-ui/react/autocomplete (Autocomplete.Root/Input/Portal/Positioner/Popup/List/Item/Group/GroupLabel/Empty/Status). Present in the dist. Direct like-for-like for the filtering command palette; Base UI's Autocomplete.Empty replaces the hand-rolled empty state.
files.priority: high — this is the largest remaining RAC collection surface and Base UI covers it

files.mixed_import: runtime `{ Button, Calendar, CalendarCell, CalendarGrid, CalendarGridBody, CalendarGridHeader, CalendarHeaderCell, DateInput, DatePicker, Dialog, Group, Popover }` from react-aria-components + `{ popoverVariants }` from ./popover.tsx
files.why_not: popoverVariants is a cva export — classnames only, no engine, no context. The rendered tree is entirely RAC and entirely self-consistent.
files.native_replacement: none exists. Base UI 1.7.0 ships no calendar, date-field, date-picker or range-calendar. The dist's top level is accordion, alert-dialog, autocomplete, avatar, button, checkbox, checkbox-group, collapsible, combobox, context-menu, dialog, direction-provider, drawer, field, fieldset, form, input, menu, menubar, meter, navigation-menu, number-field, otp-field, popover, preview-card, progress, radio, radio-group, scroll-area, select, separator, slider, switch, tabs, toast, toggle, toggle-group, toolbar, tooltip — no date primitive of any kind.
files.priority: blocking for a full migration — the date family (date-picker, date-range-picker, date-field, calendar, range-calendar) must stay on React Aria or be hand-built

files.mixed_import: runtime `{ Button, CalendarCell, CalendarGrid, CalendarGridBody, CalendarGridHeader, DateInput, DateRangePicker, Dialog, Group, Popover, RangeCalendar }` from react-aria-components + `{ popoverVariants }` from ./popover.tsx
files.why_not: same as date-picker — the only rebuilt import is a cva export

files.mixed_import: runtime `{ DropZone, FileTrigger, Text, isFileDropItem }` from react-aria-components + `{ Button, IconButton }` from ./button.tsx (rebuilt onto Base UI's Button)
files.why_not: Base UI's Button reads no context — it renders standalone anywhere. RAC's FileTrigger wraps its child in a PressResponder/ButtonContext that a Base UI Button ignores, so the ONE thing to watch is whether the picker still opens; the button renders either way. This is a silent-behaviour risk, not a throw.
files.evidence: no covering suite in the repository — measured with a throwaway probe (SSR + live render under fa-IR), both arms clean, probe deleted
files.native_replacement: none exists. Base UI ships no drop-zone and no file-trigger. A native rebuild would be a plain <input type="file"> plus hand-written drag events — i.e. not a rental at all.
files.priority: medium — verify the FileTrigger→Button press path in a browser before trusting it; it is exactly the kind of defect that renders fine and does nothing

files.mixed_import: runtime `{ Popover as AriaPopover }` from react-aria-components + `{ popoverVariants, type LumoPlacement }` from ./popover.tsx
files.why_not: the value import from the rebuilt sibling is a cva; LumoPlacement is a type. The RAC Popover is driven by this file's own useState/triggerRef, not by a RAC trigger context.
files.evidence: no covering suite — throwaway probe, both arms clean, probe deleted
files.native_replacement: @base-ui/react/preview-card (PreviewCard.Root/Trigger/Portal/Positioner/Popup/Arrow/Backdrop). Present in the dist. It is the hover-intent card by name and owns openDelay/closeDelay natively — this file's hand-written single-timer scheduler and FOCUSABLE selector both delete.
files.priority: high — a native primitive exists AND replaces ~80 lines of hand-rolled hover-intent state

files.mixed_import: runtime `{ Input as AriaInput, TextField as AriaTextField }` from react-aria-components + `{ IconButton }` from ./button.tsx
files.why_not: Base UI's Button is context-free. RAC's TextField publishes InputContext to its Input, which is RAC's own — the IconButton is a sibling addon, not a slotted participant.
files.native_replacement: @base-ui/react/input + @base-ui/react/field (Field.Root/Label/Control/Description/Error). PARTIAL: Base UI has the input and the field wiring but no grouped-addon primitive, so the addon layout stays Lumo's own composition either way.
files.priority: medium — the swap is real but buys layout nothing; do it with the rest of the form family or not at all

files.mixed_import: runtime `{ Button as AriaButton }` from react-aria-components + `{ Popover, PopoverTrigger }` from ./popover.tsx (rebuilt onto Base UI's Popover)
files.why_not: the highest-risk row in this table and it still does not throw. Lumo's PopoverTrigger lifts its first child into Base UI's Popover.Trigger `render` prop, so the RAC AriaButton is CLONED with Base UI's trigger props rather than asked for a context. It renders and it opens.
files.watch: AriaButton filters unknown DOM props. This is the exact hazard menu.tsx records as `menu.trigger-prop-forwarding` for Lumo's own Button — the trigger renders, the props may not all land. Renders green, may misbehave on data-* state styling.
files.native_replacement: @base-ui/react/navigation-menu (NavigationMenu.Root/List/Item/Trigger/Content/Portal/Positioner/Popup/Viewport/Arrow/Link/Icon). Present in the dist. Full like-for-like, and it brings the shared animated viewport this file cannot express on a plain Popover.
files.priority: high — named primitive, strictly more capable than the current composition

files.mixed_import: runtime `{ Input as AriaInput, SearchField as AriaSearchField }` from react-aria-components + `{ IconButton }` from ./button.tsx
files.why_not: Base UI's Button is context-free and renders.
files.evidence: no covering suite — throwaway probe, both arms clean, probe deleted
files.watch: SILENT BEHAVIOUR RISK, higher than file-upload's. RAC's SearchField clears itself by publishing ButtonContext with slot="clear"; a Base UI Button cannot receive a RAC slot at all (checkbox.tsx records the same gap for slot="selection"). The clear button is announced correctly, is focusable, and may do nothing. It renders green in both arms and there is no test in the repository that would catch it.
files.native_replacement: @base-ui/react/input + @base-ui/react/field. PARTIAL — Base UI has no search-field primitive; type="search", the clear button and its Persian clearLabel stay Lumo's.
files.priority: high on VERIFICATION, medium on migration — the untested clear path is the single most likely silent defect surfaced by this hunt

files.mixed_import: runtime `{ Cell, Column, ColumnResizer, ResizableTableContainer, Row, Table, TableBody, TableHeader }` from react-aria-components + `{ Checkbox }` from ./checkbox.tsx (rebuilt onto Base UI's Checkbox)
files.why_not: Base UI's Checkbox is context-free and renders inside a RAC Row/Cell without complaint.
files.evidence: src/data-display.test.tsx — passes; probe.table-selection.json already measured this pair
files.watch: KNOWN SILENT BREAK, already recorded. `<Checkbox slot="selection">` is how RAC wires row/column selection; Base UI has no slot mechanism and button.tsx documents that RAC's `slot: string | null` cannot even be spelled against Base UI's `string | undefined`. The selection checkbox renders, is announced, and is disconnected from the table's selection state.
files.native_replacement: none exists. Base UI ships no table, no collection builder, and no selection manager. The whole data-display family (table, list-box, grid-list, tag-group) has no Base UI counterpart.
files.priority: blocking for a full migration, and the slot break should be fixed or explicitly accepted NOW rather than at integrate time

files.mixed_import: runtime `{ I18nProvider, Text, UNSTABLE_Toast, UNSTABLE_ToastContent, UNSTABLE_ToastQueue, UNSTABLE_ToastRegion }` from react-aria-components + `{ IconButton }` from ./button.tsx
files.why_not: Base UI's Button is context-free; the RAC toast tree is self-consistent.
files.evidence: src/controls.test.tsx — passes (its one failure is the unrelated slider inset assertion)
files.native_replacement: @base-ui/react/toast (Toast.Provider/Portal/Viewport/Root/Title/Description/Action/Close, plus useToastManager). Present in the dist and NOT flagged unstable, unlike the RAC components this file is built on.
files.priority: high — Lumo currently depends on four UNSTABLE_-prefixed React Aria exports for a shipped component; Base UI's equivalent is stable API

excluded_and_why.reason: rebuilt. Its react-aria-components import is `import type` (DialogProps, DialogTriggerProps, HeadingProps, ModalOverlayProps) and is erased at build.
rebuilt by this pass. Its remaining react-aria-components import is now `import type { DialogProps }`, which is what keeps AlertDialogProps byte-identical to the React Aria build.

excluded_and_why.note: The type-only construction is what separates a rebuilt file from a half-migrated one. A grep for the module specifier alone cannot tell them apart and will report three false positives.

does_the_branch_build.what_remains_for_a_green_build: Nothing in these two files. Every remaining failure is a test asserting React Aria's attribute names or React Aria's defects, on a component the experiment deliberately re-engined. They are decisions for the Integrate agent — restate the vocabulary or accept the divergence — not defects to fix here. next build was NOT run (RAM budget); the CSS scanner and the RTL gate have not been exercised against the new files.
